highlights.title: OpenAI agents hijacked German website before Hugging Face hack, report claims
highlights.summary: OpenAI said it could not "meaningfully respond" to the report's findings because it hadn't been allowed to review it ahead of publication.
body: A new report claims a swarm of AI agents, developed by OpenAI, hijacked a German website - months before the firm revealed its AI had hacked tech platform Hugging Face.
The targeted website, DseWiki, is a Wikipedia-style site for programmers that its community can all contribute to.

The report is from a group called Nightingale Collective and claims that in May OpenAI's agents started using DseWiki as their own message board, shared tips on how to avoid being detected and made 15,000 edits to it.
OpenAI said it could not "meaningfully respond" to Nightingale Collective's findings because it hadn't been allowed to review the report, which was first shared with news agency Reuters.

highlights.title: Instagram’s AI detection is a mess (again)
highlights.summary: Instagram's visible AI labels are supposed to help people quickly spot synthetically generated content at a glance. Over the last few weeks, however, users have been reporting that the system has gone haywire.
body: Meta is back to adding AI labels on original photos, while not tagging AI images it should.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The precise causes of this tagging seem to vary. Many people said the label appeared on images that were edited using tools like Canva’s Background Remover or with negligible use of blemish-fixing tools. One user on Threads said Instagram was applying the label “every time there is bg remover involved,” and another user said it appeared after they used Canva to remove “a speckle” from their photo, resulting in the entire image being flagged on Instagram as AI. In other cases, the causes are even less clear.

The recently reported erroneous labels don’t have a clear link to generative AI usage. While features like background removal do often use machine learning, it’s the same assistive AI variety that apps like Photoshop have used in object selection and removal tools for over a decade — not the generative text-to-picture tools typically associated with deceptive AI imagery.
points: Instagram's visible AI labels are supposed to help people quickly spot synthetically generated content at a glance.
Over the last few weeks, however, users have been reporting that the system has gone haywire.

highlights.title: Russell tops second practice as Mercedes respond to Ferrari at Monza
highlights.summary: George Russell beat Charles Leclerc to the fastest time of second practice at the Italian Grand Prix as Mercedes responded to Ferrari's early pace at Monza.
body: At an event in which championship-leading team-mate Kimi Antonelli will start at the back of Sunday's grid owing to engine-change penalties, Russell has a big chance to eat into the Italian's 59-point advantage if he can deliver a strong race weekend.

Ferrari had finished first and second quickest in opening practice as they debuted an upgraded engine but Russell was the driver to beat in the second session amid continued sweltering temperatures in northern Italy.
The Briton set a quickest lap of 1:22.559 to outpace Leclerc - who had a late spin - by 0.120s and Antonelli by 0.141s.
Lewis Hamilton, second fastest in the earlier running, slipped to fifth behind McLaren's Lando Norris during a session which included the Ferrari running straight on at the first chicane.

highlights.title: Alien: Earth Is Officially Back as Season 2 Filming Kicks Off
highlights.summary: One of the best shows of 2025 was Alien: Earth, Noah Hawley's sci-fi horror series set in the legendary universe launched by Ridley Scott's 1979 masterpiece. Following positive reactions from critics and audiences, Disney renewed the show for a second season on Nov. 11, 2025.
body: FX posted a short video to its official Instagram account on Sept. 3, announcing that production on season 2 has begun. The video is only about ten seconds and shows some of the behind-the-scenes action on set. Production on season 1 took roughly five months, with a mid-production break due to the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike. If season 2 follows a similar schedule, it should finish production in early 2027.

Creator Noah Hawley is returning as showrunner alongside most of the cast, led by Sydney Chandler as Wendy. Season 2 will also add Peter Dinklage, Tracey Ullman, Sam Spruell, and Jerome Flynn. Hawley previously worked with Spruell on Fargo, while Dinklage and Flynn starred alongside each other in Game of Thrones.

It is a good time to be an Alien fan right now. In addition to Alien: Earth Season 2, there are at least two other major projects in the works. The 2014 game Alien: Isolation is finally getting a sequel, and it looks even scarier than the original. The game will take place on an Earth-like colony and will follow a new protagonist who is not Amanda Ripley, according to Sega.

highlights.title: Holly Throsby: ‘I was proud to not make a breakup album’
highlights.summary: The writer and musician on returning to music, finding herself, and why right now is a terrifying time to be an artist. Holly Throsby does not enjoy having her photo taken. There’s even a song on her new album about it.
body: Walking along various bush tracks is a daily ritual for Throsby. A sense of nature gently pervades her seventh album, Normal Magic. It is in the imagery of sparkling water and swims; gardens and birds; bushfires and wind and rain on the roof. The album itself feels like the breaking of a drought: her first solo record in nine years. In the intervening time, she moved to the New South Wales south coast, had her second child, wrote her third novel, and recorded and toured a second album with Seeker Lover Keeper, her collaborative project with Sarah Blasko and Sally Seltmann. She has hardly been idle.

And yet, at 47, she says “there are a lot of things, particularly if you have children, that take you away from the work. I sometimes forget that I’m an artist altogether – for long periods, years. I forget that I’m a musician.”

It’s a startling statement from someone who picked up a guitar at the age of eight. “When I was a teenager, I would get home from school and write songs all afternoon, every afternoon, obsessively,” she says. “It’s been nice to reconnect with that side of myself.”

highlights.title: Alienware’s refurbished 16 Aurora is almost $200 off at Woot
highlights.summary: Gaming laptop deals aren’t what they used to be (stares daggers at RAMageddon), which is why I consider Woot’s deal on a refurbished Alienware 16 Aurora gaming laptop with Nvidia’s RTX 5050 a pretty good deal at $927 for new Woot customers (with code WOOTALIEN used at checkout).
body: These days, most configurations with Nvidia’s RTX 5060 GPU sail well over the $1,200 mark, which is just too much if you ask me. If you’re in the market for a relatively speedy and well-designed machine, perhaps this one will be a good fit for your needs and budget. The Aurora has a 1600p 120Hz 16-inch screen, Intel’s capable Core 7 240H processor, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 512GB SSD. Its RTX 5050 GPU likely won’t be able to play most games at max settings, especially at its native 1600p resolution, but you should be able to get respectable frame rates and visual fidelity with some tweaking.

As for its condition, the company says “it’s as close to new as you can get without technically being “new.” The 16 Aurora features two M.2 slots, letting you greatly boost its included 512GB SSD with other drives. It also has two SO-DIMM slots, so you can upgrade the 8GB x 2 (DDR5 5,600MHz) down the line to 16GB x 2 (it tops out at 32GB RAM). If you have other specs you want to dig into, check out Dell’s comprehensive spec sheet within its support site.

highlights.title: Arrow gets emotional farewell on 100th Rabbitohs appearance after MND diagnosis
highlights.summary: Jai Arrow made an emotional 100th NRL appearance for the South Sydney Rabbitohs to mark his farewell from the sport, following his Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis.
body: Special dispensation had been granted by the NRL and Rabbitohs to allow Arrow the opportunity to take to the field for the opening kick-off another two times, with the game against Sydney Roosters marking a century of appearances.
Arrow walked his team out onto the field for the Sydney derby, with 'Stand By Me' playing before 'You'll Never Walk Alone' then rang around the Allianz Stadium.

The 31-year-old forward had made 178 appearances overall in the NRL before his retirement announcement earlier his year, playing at Brisbane Broncos and then Gold Coast Titans ahead of joining the Rabbitohs in 2021.
Arrow, also having featured 12 times for Queensland in State of Origin, fought back tears as he was presented to the crowd, who all stood in applause, many holding up banners of support in his name.

highlights.title: Why AI food looks like that
highlights.summary: There is a torrent of unappetizing slop coming from restaurants, cafes, and brands that are increasingly turning to AI to generate images promoting their food. The resulting horror show includes donut shrimp, Reubens from the deep, wormlike noodles, and noodle-like pastries and stringy chicken.
body: We don’t usually know why anyone would use AI slop to sell something intended to look appetizing, particularly when the food is presumably right there to photograph. But we do know a bit about why AI is so adept at producing such exquisitely nauseating images.
The model might get the basic structure of an object wrong at an earlier stage, then lump vivid texture details on top of that structure.

It doesn’t help that AI has no idea what a sandwich actually is. Or a noodle. Or a burrito. It has no understanding of the objects it’s creating or the physical world they inhabit. It has learned, broadly, what these things tend to look like on a statistical level, but not why they look that way or how they’re supposed to behave. “AI image generation reproduces looks without proper knowledge about the world,” explained Roland Meyer, a professor for digital cultures and arts at the University of Zurich in Switzerland. The result is an approximation of food divorced from any understanding of the thing itself.

Summit organizers are emphasizing the urgency of the world community to gather to address budding opportunities and structural challenges that need to be addressed through policy, contracts and trade agreements.

highlights.title: Chat to strangers and let your kids be bored: how to embrace a ‘slow September’ – and enjoy life more
highlights.summary: The pressure to self-optimise at the start of the new school year can lead to disappointment and burnout. Instead, here are seven ways to slow things down and reap the benefits. It is a hangover from our school days that September can feel like a time for getting back to the grind.
body: One antidote to this drive is to embrace a slower way of living. Rather than always rushing from one activity to the next, we could be enjoying life.

“In the age of digitisation, from work to socialising, we are seeing everything intensify,” says Heejung Chung, a professor of work and employment at King’s College London. “But by doing everything, we’re also creating a culture where it’s seen as normal. So you are not only creating a standard for yourself, but for everyone else as well. There is a creeping set of collective expectations that we can do everything, especially women, and we need to change it.”
So say “no” to self-optimisation this September, and instead embrace these practical ways to slow everything down – from work to parenting.

More often than not, we feel as though we don’t have enough time to converse with strangers in our daily lives, whether that be the woman next to you at the bus stop or the barista making your coffee. Yet taking the time to mindfully have a conversation with someone we don’t know has tangible benefits.

highlights.title: 1 vs. 100 Live Was the Kind of Incredible Creative Risk I'd Like to See Xbox Get Back To
highlights.summary: I so vividly remember making the time to log on and play 1 vs. 100 in the evenings the game was available, and trying to answer those trivia questions as quickly as possible. You could get on Party Chat with your friends and root for each other to make it into The Mob -- or even The One.
body: This is an IGN opinion piece from Ryan McCaffrey, who worked at Official Xbox Magazine from 2002-2012 during the original Xbox and Xbox 360 era before joining IGN, where he remains “the Xbox guy.” In the run-up to Xbox’s 25th anniversary, he’ll be sharing his memories from the platform’s first quarter-century.

To this day, the Achievements on my Xbox gamercard that I'm most proud of are the 12 out of 12 I got in 1 vs. 100. They are, of course, impossible to attain now, and so I will always cherish them. But 1 vs. 100 was more than a licensed video game adaptation of a popular game show. For Xbox, it was an incredibly gutsy creative risk that actually worked, and I'd love to see the company get back to that kind of boldness again.

highlights.title: Wide-legged trousers for men are having a moment. Just ask Gary Neville
highlights.summary: Neville may have been mocked for wearing them on Monday Night Football, but he is actually bang on trend. From Kylian Mbappé’s World Cup style to Erling Haaland’s hair tie, football has had many viral fashion moments in 2026.
body: Perhaps the one that speaks to the fashion crowd, and a larger debate happening in menswear right now, is Gary Neville being mercilessly teased on Sky Sports’ Monday Night Football for sporting wide-legged trousers.

As a producer played Baggy Trousers, by Madness, Neville’s chino-style, wider-legged black slacks were mocked by fellow pundit Jamie Carragher, who compared Neville to Frank Worthington, the forward from West Yorkshire whose dandyish off-pitch style raised eyebrows in the 1970s.

“I went shopping in London,” Neville explained as Carragher jogged along to the Nutty Boys’ hit. “This guy styled me. I think they’re pretty cool, you know.” He predicted that Carragher would be wearing a pair soon.
Neville seems to be on to something. Because as far as the cut of your trousers goes, girth is greater.

This would expand to include all Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock, over the next few days.

“It's something we always wanted to do,” creative director and co-founder Arcade Berg told me. “Creatively, after we were done with the first The Ascent — that was a smashing success for us — creatively, we just wanted to go somewhere else. We weren't ready to do more The Ascent there and then. And team size and also investment wise, we weren't prepared for multiple projects.

“But one of the great things that we are now working with Krafton is that we now have backing and support that we can take creative risks. So together with them, we've actually built a franchise plan. We're moving The Ascent from a game to a franchise. And we'll be dropping more news as we figure things out, because it's a longer-term plan. But it's really exciting for us to now know that we have backing and support to do more. And what that is, I can't really go into details of.”

highlights.title: AI Use in the Job Market Is Creating an Infinite Doom Loop
highlights.summary: Job seekers are trying to game the application process using AI. It’s not working, and not for the reasons you might think.
body: Jodi Beggs' résumé got dinged for being two pages long. She used her middle initial on one document but not another, which also cost her points. If she changed “percent” to the % sign, her score went up.

Beggs, a data scientist and job seeker, got this feedback from an online system that compares a job description with an applicant's materials to assess how well they match up. The most well known of these tools is Jobscan, though Beggs didn't say which one she tested.
“If my job is to please the robots,” Beggs says, “then even if I don't like AI-generated content, maybe the machines do.”

Jobscan and other apps like it work on the premise that hiring committees use AI to automatically rate and rank candidates in their applicant tracking system (ATS). Only the top 10 to 20 percent of applicants are considered. The bottom 80 might never see the light of day. That's the belief, anyway. To get on the short list, candidates must tailor the formatting of their CVs and cover letters and pack them with the right keywords to match what the ATS wants to see.

highlights.title: Data from drones in Ukraine is fueling a new Wild West marketplace
highlights.summary: Battlefields in Ukraine are littered with the remnants of drones, which are now firmly established as a critical weapon of modern warfare. But behind all that wreckage, there’s a new gold mine for the defense sector.
body: For every flight, unmanned systems collect thousands of points of data, from images and video to controller inputs. Together, those records show how a machine and a person responded to constantly shifting circumstances.

Ukraine has now begun converting that experience into a resource. Its Ministry of Defense announced in January that it would make millions of data points gathered during tens of thousands of drone flights available to both military contractors and commercial companies, and since then more than 100 companies and the UK government have gained access.

For a country at war, it’s a quick way to attract funding and partnerships. But this step turns the front line into an active site of model training, taking advantage of how the chaos of war creates conditions that AI companies struggle to reproduce on their own.

Other countries and battlefields are likely to follow Ukraine’s lead, but the responsibility for governing this new industry cannot fall solely on a country fighting for its survival. That legal vacuum has to be filled together by the countries and companies involved in this industry’s development.

She was the singing voice for Princess Jasmine in “Aladdin” as well as Fa Mulan in “Mulan” and “Mulan 2.” Later this month, Salonga, who made her singing debut when she was just seven years old in her native Manila, appears in “Forgotten Island,” DreamWorks Animation’s Philippines-set fantasy adventure about childhood friends who get trapped in the mystical world of Nakali.

“It centers on my culture,” Salonga tells me over a Zoom video call earlier this week. “It centers Philippine myth and folklore. We get to share our mythological creatures with the bigger world. I don’t think it’s something that I ever thought I would have seen.”

Salonga’s work as Kim earned her a Laurence Olivier Award and in 1991, she became the first Asian actress to win a Tony Award and the second-youngest actress to win for best performance by a leading actress in a musical.

highlights.title: Unzipped: The Oral History
highlights.summary: As this beloved documentary heads back to cinemas, Isaac Mizrahi, Douglas Keeve, and Nina Santisi—the film’s star, director, and producer, respectively, tell Vogue how it all came together back in 1995.
body: “Good news is good news and bad news is good news when you make a documentary,” observes Douglas Keeve, who directed Unzipped, the iconic fashion film that has been restored to be rereleased in theaters 31 years after its 1995 release. “It’s just about discovery, you know. You have to be a journalist, but you have to be innocent too. And try not to steer it, just try to capture it.”
Life might sometimes be stranger than fiction, but all storytellers—be they fantasists or documentarians—need some kind of action to propel their narratives forward.

The grain of sand around which Keeve forms his rare pearl of a movie is the negative fashion review designer Isaac Mizrahi, the film’s extrovert subject, received for his spring 1994 ready-to-wear collection. What follows is an examination of the largely associative and intuitive process by which the designer is driven to create a fall lineup that will bring the critics back around to his side.
